description: Given a collection of numbers, nums, that might contain duplicates, return all possible unique permutations in any order.
examples:
Input: nums = [1, 1, 2]
Output: [[1,1,2],[1,2,1],[2,1,1]]
Explanation: Only three unique permutations exist because the two 1s are indistinguishable.
intuition: When you have duplicate elements, swapping two identical items produces the same permutation. The trick is to sort the array and enforce a rule: among identical values, always use them in left-to-right order. If a duplicate's predecessor was not used at the current level, skip it -- this single rule eliminates all duplicate permutations.
approach: Sort the array so duplicates are adjacent. Use backtracking with a used-index set and skip a duplicate element if the previous identical element at the same level was not used. This ensures each duplicate is only used in one fixed order.
jsWalkthrough:
nums = [1, 1, 2]
After sort: [1, 1, 2]  (indices 0,1,2)

backtrack([])
  i=0: nums[0]=1, used=[F,F,F] → place 1, used=[T,F,F]
    i=0: used[0]=true → skip
    i=1: nums[1]=1, nums[0]=1, used[0]=true → NOT skipped (used[i-1] is true)
          place 1 → current=[1,1], used=[T,T,F]
      i=2: place 2 → current=[1,1,2] → push [1,1,2]
    i=2: place 2 → current=[1,2], used=[T,F,T]
      i=1: nums[1]=1, nums[0]=1, used[0]=true → place 1 → [1,2,1] → push
  i=1: nums[1]=1, nums[0]=1, used[0]=false → SKIP (dedup)
  i=2: nums[2]=2 → place 2, used=[F,F,T]
    i=0: place 1 → current=[2,1], used=[T,F,T]
      i=1: nums[1]=1, used[0]=true → place 1 → [2,1,1] → push

result = [[1,1,2],[1,2,1],[2,1,1]]
explanation:
- Sort nums so duplicates are adjacent, making it easy to detect and skip them.
- used is a boolean array tracking whether each index is currently in the permutation.
- The deduplication condition: if nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1], skip. This enforces that among duplicates, we always pick them in left-to-right order.
- The rest follows standard permutation backtracking: mark used, append, recurse, pop, unmark.
spaceComplexity: O(n) for the recursion stack and used array
hints: Sort the array first so that duplicate values are adjacent.
The key insight is to skip a duplicate if the previous identical value was not used at this recursion level -- this forces a canonical ordering among duplicates.
Use a boolean used array indexed by position to track which elements are in the current permutation.

phases.label: Scan candidate indices across partial permutations

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: All-distinct values give the largest search tree. Sorting enables duplicate pruning but does not change that worst-case bound.
